summary: Re-ran M5-S01's declared molecular tests against the F-49/F-50 rebuild (metadata-builder, 2026-09-12T10-08-00Z; set built by build-step-runner at 10-12-00Z). The prior tested record (09-50-00Z) was against the pre-rebuild report the org rejected and is now superseded. All 6 XML files parsed; the manifest was structurally consistent (5 members across ListView and Report, each covered by a file, each file mapping to a member, no wildcards); check_list_views_and_compact_layouts.py at build scope exited 0 ('No issues found.'); check_report_inventory.py at step scope exited 0 (score 100, 'Scanned 1 report/dashboard file(s); 0 finding(s) detected.'); check-outputs returned ok with no missing/empty/malformed paths. The one declared manual test (Given/When/Then, queue-name cross-check plus the Tier 1 interim-view claim) names observable outcomes and was recorded verbatim for the milestone gate rather than ticked. 0 failures; step moved built -> tested. Test-coverage finding for this run specifically: both declared checkers returned the identical exit-0/score-100 verdict on the pre-rebuild report the org rejected and on the rebuilt report the org has not yet re-validated -- neither checker asserts anything about reportType, columns, groupingsDown or description length, so this step's green automated gates carry no signal on the four fields F-49/F-50 changed.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran (two checkers, both always-on checks) or was correctly classified as manual; both checkers exist and were invoked verbatim with no flag rewritten; every exit code and check-outputs result was observed directly by this run rather than assumed from the prior envelopes.

process_observations.observation: Both declared checkers passed cleanly on the first invocation this run, with no repairs or re-runs needed, and check-outputs confirmed all 6 declared outputs present, non-empty and well-formed on the rebuilt artefact set.

Both declared checkers score identically (exit 0, list-view checker 'No issues found.', report checker 100/0 findings) on the pre-rebuild report the org rejected for a >255-char description and an invalid reportType/grouping, and on the rebuilt report that fixed those fields. Neither check_list_views_and_compact_layouts.py nor check_report_inventory.py asserts anything about a Report's description length, reportType value, or column/grouping exclusivity, so a step-tester green run on this step's report has never carried evidence that the file is deployable -- only that it is well-formed and inventoried. This is the tester's own observation on this run's own two checker invocations, not merely a carry-forward of the metadata-builder/build-step-runner envelopes' finding.

The step reaches tested a second time with its report still shipping without the Escalated criterion that gives it its purpose (Q91): no cited skill carries a report column code for Case.IsEscalated, so the report as written returns open Cases from the last 30 days rather than escalated open Cases, and neither declared checker can detect a missing filter criterion.

The declared folder filename reports/Support_Operations-meta.xml does not match the .reportFolder-meta.xml form check_report_inventory.py's FOLDER_SUFFIXES recognises, so acceptance_tests[1]'s folder-sharing assertion never executes inside that checker even though the test exits 0 (Scanned 1 file, not 2); this run's own manifest check treated the file as consistent with package.xml based on its <ReportFolder> content rather than its filename, which is a judgment call for the milestone gate to affirm or overturn. Unlike the checker's blind spot, this one is now moot for deployability: MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 1 validated the folder against the org at this exact declared filename.

The manual acceptance test bundles two distinct observable outcomes (each view's <queue> resolving under artefacts/M2-S04/queues/, and the Tier 1 General view's presence as an interim surface) into one Given/When/Then line, which a human ticks as a single unit even though the second clause is a standing policy note rather than a per-file check.

M5-S01 is tested again with three findings the M5 gate has not yet adjudicated (the absent Escalated criterion, the folder filename/checker mismatch, and this run's test-coverage finding that both checkers are blind to the report body's deployability-relevant fields); build-doc-keeper should carry all three into decisions.md before the gate.
process_observations.followup_reason: because it is the agent that records step findings into decisions.md ahead of a milestone gate, and none of the three findings has a decisions.md entry yet.
